title: What numbers do the sides of regular polygons follow?
description: The sides of the regular polygons from a triangle to a decagon are counted, and the counts are matched with the names of the shapes. Keeko doubts this and says the sides should start at one.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number of sides runs through the counting numbers starting at three, and each count gives the name of the shape. Watch for students who think the row should start at one side.

source: The number of sides in the shape sequence of Regular Polygons is given by the counting numbers starting at 3.
video_script.why: The child learns to count the sides of the regular polygons of the book, see which numbers they make, and name each shape from its number of sides.
video_script.substitution: The regular polygons of the book are counted, from three sides up to ten sides.
video_script.anchor: a row of regular polygons with the number of sides written under each
video_script.wrong_answer: the sides should start at one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the sides should start at one, since counting starts at one. One side is only a line that never closes, and two sides leave a gap, so the smallest closed shape has three sides and the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The sides are the counting numbers starting at three

final_answer.value: the sides 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 are the counting numbers starting at 3; the names are triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon, decagon
final_answer.spoken: the counting numbers starting at three

maths_rules: a regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal
the sides of the regular polygons are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10
each count is 1 more than the one before, with no number skipped
3 triangle, 4 quadrilateral, 5 pentagon, 6 hexagon, 7 heptagon, 8 octagon, 9 nonagon, 10 decagon
a closed shape needs at least 3 sides
video_script.design: A row of regular polygons stands on the board with the side counts under them. The counts are read as a pattern, and then each shape gets its name.

<bookmark mark='row'/>Here is a row of them, with three sides, four sides, five sides and more.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What numbers do their sides follow, and what are the shapes called?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='reg'/>A shape with all sides equal and all angles equal is called a regular polygon.
<bookmark mark='count'/>We can count the sides of each one to find the numbers.

marks.count: the sides of each shape are lit one by one and the count is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step one, count the sides of each regular polygon in the row. The counts are three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine and ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the pattern: start at 3, up by 1 each time, no number skipped

marks.start: a ring is drawn round the first count, three

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step two, look at how the counts change. They start at three.
<bookmark mark='plus'/>Each count is one more than the one before, and no number is skipped.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the names: 3 triangle, 4 quadrilateral (a square), 5 pentagon, 6 hexagon, 7 heptagon, 8 octagon, 9 nonagon, 10 decagon

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, give each shape its name from its number of sides. Three sides make a triangle, and four sides make a quadrilateral.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Five sides make a pentagon, six make a hexagon, and seven make a heptagon.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Eight sides make an octagon, nine make a nonagon, and ten make a decagon.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the sides 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 are the counting numbers starting at 3; the names follow from them

marks.ans: the counts and the names are boxed together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sides are the counting numbers starting at three. The name of each shape follows from its number of sides.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says the sides start at 1; a single line and a pair of lines are drawn, and neither is closed; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.one: a single line is drawn, and it does not close
marks.two: two lines are drawn, and a gap is left between their ends
marks.strike: a triangle closes the gap and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the sides should start at one, since counting starts at one.
<bookmark mark='one'/>One side is only a line, and it never closes into a shape.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two sides still leave a gap between their ends.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The smallest closed shape needs three sides, so the row starts at three.
